title: Aspect-aware vignette pass
purpose: Darken or tint a three.js frame toward its edges with a smooth band between two radii, round in pixels or shaped like the frame, as a shader definition for ShaderPass or a full-screen ShaderMaterial, with an exact CPU mirror of the falloff. Use it to frame shots and pull the eye to the centre.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (the shader includes the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createVignetteShader
exports.summary: A fresh shader definition for three.js ShaderPass or ShaderMaterial; vector uniforms are plain arrays.

exports.name: createVignetteMaterial
exports.summary: The definition as a full-screen ShaderMaterial without depth test or write.

exports.name: vignetteAmount
exports.summary: CPU mirror: how far the pixel at uv is mixed toward the vignette colour, from 0 to strength.

options.name: color
options.meaning: Colour the edges are mixed toward.

options.name: inner
options.meaning: Distance where the falloff starts (0 centre, 1 middle of the top edge).

options.name: outer
options.meaning: Distance where the falloff reaches strength; not smaller than inner.

options.name: roundness
options.meaning: 1 measures distance in pixels (a round vignette), 0 stretches it with the frame.

options.name: aspect
options.meaning: Frame width over height; update uAspect when the canvas is resized.

limits: A colour mix, not a lens model: no optical falloff, chromatic shift or exposure change. The pass reads one texture and writes one, so it needs a render target or an EffectComposer in front of it. uAspect is not updated by itself: set it when the canvas is resized. The output goes through three.js's output colour space conversion, so as the last pass it writes sRGB to the screen and into a linear render target it writes linear values. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Aspect-corrected radial distance blended with frame-shaped distance
